The intermeeting 50 bp cut to a 1.00–1.25% target range, paired with lowering IOER to 1.10% and continuing T-bill purchases and repo operations, is consistent with acting preemptively amid rising downside risks. The FSR backdrop reinforces this approach: it highlighted elevated valuation pressures and high business leverage, as well as vulnerabilities in short‑term funding markets underscored by the September 2019 repo episode. By maintaining ample reserves and active Desk operations, the Fed directly addresses those funding risks and supports transmission. At the same time, the FSR noted that bank capital and liquidity were solid and household credit quality remained relatively strong, suggesting the system had buffers to absorb stress. Net assessment: risk-aware and decisively accommodative policy that mitigates market-functioning risks, but with a cautious near-term outlook given preexisting vulnerabilities and the evolving COVID-19 shock.
